key_insight: LaviGen repurposes pretrained 3D generative models to perform autoregressive layout generation directly in native 3D space, explicitly modeling geometric relations and physical constraints to produce coherent, physically plausible 3D scenes.
problem_solved: Existing layout generation approaches often rely on text or 2D proxies and fail to explicitly enforce 3D geometric relations and physical feasibility; LaviGen addresses the challenge of generating coherent, physically-plausible object layouts in true 3D space.
method: Formulate layout generation as an autoregressive process in native 3D space: sequentially place objects conditioned on previously placed objects and relations.
Repurpose pretrained 3D generative models and adapt a 3D diffusion model for sampling and refinement of object placements within the autoregressive pipeline.
Explicitly model geometric relations and physical constraints (e.g., support, collision avoidance, alignment) during generation to ensure scene coherence and plausibility.
impact: Produces more realistic 3D scenes without heavy post-processing, benefiting simulation, robotics, AR/VR, and content creation workflows by reducing manual correction and improving physical fidelity of generated layouts.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing autoregressive placement loop + adapted 3D diffusion refinement
Side-by-side 3D scenes: naive/random layout vs. LaviGen-generated physically-plausible layout
3D scene with relation-overlay (support, adjacency, collision edges) to highlight constraints
Comparison chart illustrating benefits of native 3D autoregressive approach vs. text- or 2D-driven methods
paper_title: Repurposing 3D Generative Model for Autoregressive Layout Generation
paper_authors: Haoran Feng, Yifan Niu, Zehuan Huang, Yang-Tian Sun, Chunchao Guo
